children: New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- HDFC Bank, India's largest private sector lender, on Saturday announced its financial results for the second quarter of FY27, reporting a 5.2% year-on-year (YoY) increase in standalone net profit to Rs.19,609.96 crore.

The bank's profit after tax (PAT) was Rs.18,641.28 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. On a sequential basis, net profit grew 2.83% from Rs.19,069.72 crore in the June 2026 quarter.

Net interest income (NII), which represents the difference between interest earned and interest expended, increased 9.72% YoY to Rs.34,619.18 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs.31,551.50 crore in the year-ago quarter. Total interest earned during the quarter stood at Rs.83,426.60 crore.
The bank's net interest margin (NIM) stood at 3.16% on total assets and 3.32% on interest-earning assets.

The quarter is also significant as it is expected to be the final earnings report under managing director and chief executive officer Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose tenure ends on October 26. Anup Bagchi is set to replace him.
HDFC Bank Q2 Results: Asset quality improves

HDFC Bank reported an improvement in its gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio, which declined to 1.11% of gross advances as of September 30, 2026. This compared with 1.17% in the preceding quarter and 1.24% in the year-ago period.
The net non-performing asset (NNPA) ratio remained stable at 0.37%, indicating that the bank's reported net bad-loan ratio was unchanged.
